Housing, water, sewerage, solid waste, grievance and revenue records for six cities in five states, joined on one property identifier and readable at Union, State and city level.

Completed units with a verified utility identifier as a share of completed units. Lowest share first.

› › Data and evidence

Data provenance and conflicts

Source coverage by register

Coverage is the share of records in that register carrying an attached source document. Reported per register, because the weakest register limits the decision.

Record conflicts

A material conflict changes what a decision maker would conclude. An informational conflict is a register hygiene issue that does not change the reading.

Reading rules applied throughout

Observed values come from service records. Reported values come from delivery and asset registers. The two are never combined into a single score or index.

Physical completion is never presented as service delivery. Where both exist for the same project they appear as separate columns.

Every figure names the records behind it, so a reader can call for the underlying record rather than accept the number.

Conflicts are published rather than resolved silently, so the register's weaknesses are visible to the same officer who reads its outputs.

› How this works

How this works

The five layers, what changes against present practice, the effect on conditional transfers, and the steps a State would take to adopt it.

The five layers

Read bottom up. Each layer depends only on the one below, so a state or a mission can adopt part of the stack without adopting all of it.

1. Identifier

A single property identifier, minted when a plot enters the urban register and carried for the life of the property through construction, connection, occupancy, assessment and grievance.

Effect: mission beneficiary lists resolve to the same property record, so reconciliation between them is not a separate exercise.

2. Registries

Six registries held by their existing custodians: project, asset, connection, revenue, grievance, and contract with liability. No register moves, no custodian changes, and each remains the authority for its own fields.

Effect: the city keeps its records. The state and the Union read a view over them, not a copy of them.

3. Interoperability

Published schemas and a resolution service, so a query can cross registries on the identifier. This is the only layer that is new build.

Effect: a sewage complaint resolves to an asset, the asset to a contract, the contract to a liability period, in one hop each.

4. Rules and events

Conditions expressed once and evaluated at the point of approval. An occupancy certificate does not issue where no connection identifier exists. A release does not clear where no service record exists.

Effect: the condition is applied on submission rather than at audit. The holds and clearances in this prototype are rule outcomes, not manual instructions.

5. Views

City, state and Union views over the same records, each showing what that level can act on.

Effect: a new view is a small piece of work once the identifier and the rules exist. Without them, no view can reconstruct the missing link.

What changes in practice

Left, the position this prototype assumes today. Right, what the shared identifier makes available.

Present practice

  • Each mission runs its own management information system with its own beneficiary list.
  • Completion is reported as achievement. Whether the household has water is a separate enquiry, usually a field visit.
  • Utilisation certificates are compiled manually and cleared on documentation rather than on service.
  • A citizen complaint reaches a department, not the contractor who carries the defect liability.
  • Reconciling city, state and central figures is itself a workstream.
  • Adding a mission means adding a portal, a login and a reporting format.

With a shared identifier

  • One register of properties, read by every mission, with mission tags rather than mission silos.
  • Completion and connection are separate fields on the same record, so the gap is visible without a visit.
  • Release conditions are evaluated against the service record at the point of release.
  • A complaint resolves to an asset, a contract and a liability window, and routes to the party who must rectify at their own cost.
  • One number, held once, read at three levels.
  • Adding a mission means publishing a schema against an identifier that already exists.

Effect on conditional transfers

Urban transfers are conditional in design. In practice the condition is checked against paper submitted after the fact. A shared identifier allows the same condition to be checked against a record at the moment of release, without a new inspection regime and without amending the guidelines.

The chain this prototype demonstrates runs in one direction and can be read in either. A delayed water main leaves completed houses without a connection identifier. The absence of that identifier stops the occupancy certificate, which stops the tax assessment, which stops the final tranche. The rule evaluates on the record.

Read downward, the same chain gives the Union a question it can put precisely: which properties are complete and unserved, and which agency owns the dependency that left them so.

MoHUA Urban DPI Prototype | Built for presentation to MoHUA

All observations, identifiers, financial values and contractor names in this prototype are synthetic. They demonstrate the structure of a shared urban registry and are not official statistics. Base geography is schematic and is not a survey boundary. Government records remain the authoritative source.
